meta.description: Events that can happen on the cultivation timeline (day 0-33). Each event is written from chunks in vector_db (data/json/total_RAG.json). The engine does not read this file yet.
rules: Verdicts, probabilities and numeric effects are game values set by the team, not measurements. The chunks only say what happened.
Crisis events point to evidence.json with crisis_ref. Their trigger, symptoms, actions and numbers stay in evidence.json; this file adds only the timeline window and DB chunks.
Night drift still applies once per game day (milestones). Cultivation days between milestones only check events, so the current balance does not change.
Every value marked draft needs a team answer before the engine uses it.
parallel_tracks are dated records from real experiments, shown beside the player's run as measured records. They never change verdicts or numbers.

events.summary: VEG-01A and VEG-01B lettuce stopped growing around day 14-15; the reservoir was not giving the pillows enough water, and the crew added water directly to the pillows.
open_questions: evidence.json cites Massa, Dufour, Smith (2014) for this crisis. veg01-stall-a/b (opag-2017-0003) give the day numbers and the recovery outcome; should they replace or join that source?

events.summary: Poor air circulation leaves droplets on leaves, a micro environment favorable for microbes. In VEG-03A the fan read 'low' after a power cycle but was off, and early seedlings had excess moisture.
open_questions: The DB has no chunk for the zinnia mold record (VEG-01C) that evidence.json uses for the symptom stages. Keep the zinnia sources, or rewrite the crisis around the fan and droplet chunks?

events.name: Open the germination wicks
events.summary: Three days after initiation, astronauts used forceps to spread the wicks apart so seedlings could emerge.
events.scene_hint: Small shoots press against the wicks of each pillow.
draft: All verdicts and effects. The sources record the procedure only, not what happens when it is skipped.

events.name: Thin to one plant per pillow
events.summary: On day 7, seedlings were thinned so each pillow kept one plant. In VEG-01A one pillow never germinated and was left out of thinning.
draft: All verdicts and effects. No source measures the effect of skipping thinning.

events.name: Harvest and freeze the samples
events.summary: VEG-01A and B were harvested after 33 days with sanitized scissors. Research samples were wrapped in sterile foil, bagged and frozen at -80 °C until return.
draft: No new rules. This event only links the existing harvest and freeze phases to DB chunks for the text.

events.name: Water does not enter a pillow
events.summary: At initiation of VEG-01A, pillow A could not be hydrated, thought to be a blocked quick disconnect or internal tube, and was swapped. In VEG-01B the same pillow failed again; ground analysis later found the internal fill tube clogged.
events.scene_hint: Water is added, but one pillow stays dry and light.

on_occur.note: While water_blocked is set, water care ops add nothing to root moisture, so the night drift can lead to water_shortage.

draft: Whether water_blocked should also clear by itself after some days.

events.name: The fan reads low but is off
events.summary: In VEG-03A, after power was cycled to Veggie, the fan read 'low' but was actually off. Seedlings had excess moisture early in growth; the same anomaly had caused excess moisture in an earlier zinnia test.
events.scene_hint: The panel shows fan LOW, but the leaves do not move and droplets stay on them.

on_occur.note: While fan_actually_off is set, night drift adds extra humidity, so overwater_mold becomes likely.

draft: probability, verdicts, effects and the extra night drift (+5 humidity)
Whether fan_high should clear the flag (the source does not say restarting at a new setting fixes it).

events.name: Leaf tips look slightly burnt
events.summary: In VEG-03J, some plants showed mild tip burn after germination, which the authors describe as indicative of rapid growth.
events.scene_hint: The edges of a few young leaves look slightly brown.
draft: This event teaches that a visible change is not always a crisis; confirm the team wants a no-harm event.

entries.text: Pillow A could not be hydrated and was swapped with a spare pillow.
Pillow B never germinated; the other pillows were thinned to one seedling each.
Three of five plants were stunted; the crew added water directly to the pillows. One recovered and two died.
Harvest planned for day 28 was moved to day 33 because of the low-water growth.
Pillows and reservoir were watered; after that, water was added directly to the pillows at every scheduled watering.
The plants recovered and were harvested.
The fan read 'low' after a power cycle but was off; seedlings had excess moisture.
Astronauts spread the wicks apart with forceps to help seedlings emerge.
Seedlings were thinned so each pillow kept one viable seedling.
Some plants showed mild tip burn, a sign of rapid growth.
Plants were harvested; tissue was wrapped, bagged and frozen at -80 °C until return.
